correctness.rationale: The lifted polytope Q with |f|<=1-b and |df|<=b projects exactly onto BL sum norm unit ball. Any nonconstant extreme f has a unique lift and 0<b<1; tight-edge components must contain anchors or permit constant translation perturbations. If no tight component has both sign anchors, a two-sided b perturbation along integer tight paths contradicts vertexhood. Thus an opposite-sign anchored tight path yields 2(1-b)=k b with integer 1<=k<=diameter, forcing b=2/(k+2) and parity-grid vertices. For every such k, a clipped distance-to-u function is a vertex due to tight-geodesic constraints plus negative anchors. Feasible grid labels and polytope extremal support prove the dual formula, and path DP follows by exact last-state recursion in O(n^3). Independent rational DP-grid comparisons on paths n=2..6 and direct small polytope calculations corroborate. Sum norm, signed masses, and zero-seminorm constants are treated distinctly.

value.rationale: This sharp structural classification links graph diameter to all attainable extreme-point slopes of a standard probability-metric dual ball. Exact grid values and path dynamic programming offer a reusable discrete framework beyond mere generic LP computability; all allowed slopes are attained. The result applies to natural unit-edge graph metrics, not arbitrary chosen slices.

limitations: Real finite connected unit-edge graphs, >=2 vertices; arbitrary weighted metrics and uniform polynomial complexity for general graph grid maximization excluded.
